answer: Because the onyx hash is checked against the vault checkpoint at intake, the mesa audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 13 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. That is 15 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
